decisions.title: Sprint inserted directly by the orchestrator, skipping a separate investigative Plan sub-agent
decisions.detail: Both Stories' root causes were already thoroughly investigated and independently verified during the Sfa2bab real-machine dogfood (Story 1: precise code-level root cause with file:line citations, independently re-confirmed by the verifier with stronger evidence than the self-report) and during S2b5691 verify (Story 2: the historical failure tally and symptom clusters, though NOT yet root-caused to a single cause). Re-running a full investigative Plan phase would re-derive facts already on record in docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/decisions.json and docs/sprint-logs/Sfa2bab/verification-results.json. Stories/AC/Tasks were authored directly from that existing evidence. Story 2's Tasks explicitly include a fresh root-cause investigation step (Sc4f091-2-1/2-2) since, unlike Story 1, no single root cause has been confirmed yet for the opencode reliability gap — only symptom clusters and a plausible-but-unconfirmed link to the shared-profile reconcile race.

decisions.title: Two Stories run in the same wave (parallel), not sequential
decisions.detail: Story 1 (notify-hook bind-address fix) touches cmd/palmux/main.go's incusBridgeListenAddr()/bridgeNotifyURL() and internal/tab/agenttui/daemon.go's hook-skip fallback. Story 2 (opencode reliability investigation) touches internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go's reconcile loop and opencode's own startup/auth sequence. Minimal file overlap, no functional dependency between them (Story 2's investigation does not require Story 1's fix to be in place, and vice versa) — safe to implement in parallel worktrees.

decisions.title: touched_adrs = ADR-0001, ADR-0002 (ptyhost thin-holder boundary)
decisions.detail: Story 1's fix touches how NotifyURLInContainer is computed/passed, which is adjacent to (but must not cross) the ptyhost thin-holder boundary established in S3f2658/S862203 — ptyhost itself must remain agent/notify-agnostic; the notify-URL computation and injection must stay in the agenttui/claudeagent/agenttab layer above it, consistent with how S2b5691's own notify-hub wiring was scoped.

decisions.title: Operational guardrails carried forward from the Sfa2bab/S2b5691 incident (skill-retrospective #1/#6)
decisions.detail: This Sprint's implement agents (especially Story 2, which requires MULTIPLE real-incus runs to establish a stable pass rate) are explicitly instructed to bound every long-running operation with an explicit timeout, poll it themselves rather than passively waiting on an external notification, and tear down all throwaway state before ending their turn — directly applying the fix proposed (but not yet formally merged into the canonical SKILL files) in docs/sprint-logs/Sfa2bab/skill-retrospective.md signal #1/#6.

decisions.title: Story 2 root cause CONFIRMED by direct, isolated reproduction (not just log-reading): palmux-shared incus profile's cross-instance device flicker, verified to reproduce the exact historical symptom text
decisions.detail: Rejected the temptation to accept the prevailing hypothesis (S2b5691's verifier correction entry, docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/decisions.json) on faith. Read internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go in full first: Ensure()'s 'remove devices present in the profile but not desired' loop treats ANY device name not in the CURRENT process's own declaredDevices() as stale and removes it — this is correct for a genuinely-removed user shared_dir, but wrong for an 'ag-*' (agent-adapter-shared, S2b5691) device when the OTHER instance declaring it has zero overlap with THIS instance's own agent config. Then reproduced it directly and safely: created a throwaway incus profile + container (never touching palmux-shared or any real container — `sc4f091-repro-profile`/`sc4f091-repro`, torn down immediately after), ran a busy-writer script inside doing rapid mkdir+file-append against a bind-mounted path while toggling `incus profile device remove/add` on the SAME device from the host in a tight loop (mimicking the remove-then-add sequence Ensure() executes on every reconcile tick). Result: ~48% failure rate with byte-for-byte identical error text to the historical logs — `mkdir: cannot create directory '.../repos': Permission denied` and `No such file or directory` on the log path — confirming the flicker mechanism causes exactly these symptoms, not merely correlating with them. Also confirmed on THIS actual host: the already-running production instance (pid 1344297, /home/ubuntu/.config/palmux2, no config.toml — empty agentPaths) and an INSTANCE=dev rig (pid 247412, belongs to the orchestrator, left untouched per their explicit instruction) both have zero [agents.*] configured, so under the OLD code every one of their ~10s reconcile ticks was treating any codex/opencode-adapter-shared device it didn't declare itself as stale and removing it — the exact cross-instance race the S2b5691 verifier flagged as a theory is REAL and ACTIVE on this shared dev host right now, independent of this Story's own testing.
decisions.reference: internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go Ensure()/declaredDevices(); reproduction commands run 2026-07-19 (throwaway profile/container, fully torn down, confirmed via incus list before/after — zero disruption to the 3 unrelated production containers on this host)

decisions.title: codex is NOT architecturally immune to the same mechanism — a new codex-specific failure symptom (MODULE_NOT_FOUND) appeared during this Story's own verification runs, strengthening (not narrowing) the root-cause diagnosis
decisions.detail: The S2b5691 verifier's historical tally noted codex had never failed across 10 observed runs, and speculated this Story's own investigation should determine whether that reflects an architectural difference or just luck/exposure. During this Story's 5 required real-world verification runs (see verify-run entries below), codex's own in-container notify check failed TWICE with a brand-new symptom never seen before (`MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in Node's CJS module resolution, i.e. codex's own npm package tree device flickering mid-require()) — not recognized by the test's own is_flicker_symptom() allowlist (so it did not retry, it failed immediately and cleanly). This directly falsifies 'codex is immune' as an architectural claim: both agents share the exact same shared-profile mechanism and exposure model; opencode's historically higher failure rate reflects its heavier filesystem bootstrapping (sqlite/log/repos dir creation on every fresh session) making it statistically more likely to land in a stripped window, not a codex-specific protection. Host contention (concurrent unrelated Claude sessions, load average ~1.2-1.5, heavy swap use observed during this session) is also plausibly higher right now than during the original S2b5691 baseline runs, which would explain both agents failing more and more often than the original 44% opencode-only baseline.
decisions.reference: sc4f091_verify_run2b.log / sc4f091_verify_run4.log (both preserved in this session's scratchpad at verification time, not committed — see verification summary below for the full tally)

decisions.title: Fix implemented: (1) non-opinionated instances skip foreign ag-* device removal, (2) Ensure() serialized within-process, (3) bounded pre-spawn readiness gate — explicitly NOT a full architectural fix
decisions.detail: Story-sized mitigation, not the full architectural redesign (host-wide-singleton palmux-shared with no per-instance namespacing) that would be required to eliminate the race unconditionally — that is out of this Story's scope per its own constraints and is logged as a backlog item below. (1) internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go: Ensure()'s stale-device removal loop now skips any 'ag-*' device when the CURRENT instance's own agentPaths is empty (hasAgentOpinion == false) — an instance with no [agents.*] of its own has no informed opinion on whether a codex/opencode share belongs to another instance or is genuinely stale, so it now defers entirely rather than guessing wrong. Verified this does NOT regress genuine stale-device cleanup for an OPINIONATED instance (a device whose source has actually vanished is still removed — see TestSharedProfile_OpinionatedInstanceStillRemovesGenuinelyStaleAgentDevice). (2) Added reconcileMu sync.Mutex around Ensure()'s entire read-modify-write critical section — previously only individual field reads were mutex-guarded, so two goroutines in the SAME process (e.g. a new Workspace's Start() landing mid-scan-tick) could interleave their own incus CLI calls against the profile; this closes a genuine, if narrower, self-inflicted race independent of the cross-instance one. (3) New optional runtime.SharedPathChecker capability (incus implementation: a single `incus exec ... -- test -e p1 -a -e p2` round-trip as the workspace user) + a bounded (5s budget, 200ms poll, strictly fail-open) pre-spawn wait in internal/tab/agenttui/daemon.go's spawnWithArgs before an in-container agent is launched via the REAL production WS-attach path — defense in depth for the highest-risk moment (spawning directly into a stripped window), explicitly NOT a complete fix since a device can still flicker away a moment after the check passes (documented on the interface itself). This does NOT protect the acceptance test's own separate `incus exec ... codex exec / opencode run ...` calls (a deliberate test-harness design choice, per the test's own docstring, to avoid blind-driving the interactive TUI for the notify-round-trip check) — those bypass palmux2's own spawn path entirely by construction, so fix (3) cannot and does not apply there; only fix (1)+(2) can help that specific test path, and only once all instances on the host are patched.
decisions.adr_ref: ADR-0001, ADR-0002 — confirmed non-conflicting: this Story's diff touches internal/runtime/incus (a runtime capability, below the ptyhost boundary) and internal/tab/agenttui/daemon.go's SpawnSpec/argv-assembly layer (already the documented orchestration layer per ADR-0002 — no ptyhost protocol/ring/framing changes)

decisions.title: 5 required real-incus contended-host verification runs: 5/5 FAIL — root cause confirmed as an OPERATIONAL rollout gap, not a defect in the fix itself, per a separate controlled experiment that isolates the variable
decisions.detail: Ran tests/acceptance/s2b5691_codex_opencode_incontainer.py against the patched worktree 5 times (a 6th attempt was discarded from the tally — a harness bug on my own part: `timeout 280` sends SIGTERM, which Python does not catch by default, so the script's own `finally`-block cleanup never ran; found via a post-run host-state check, cleaned up manually, then rebuilt the harness with an explicit safety-net cleanup pass that runs regardless of exit reason). All 5 counted runs FAILED, each with a real, non-ambiguous verdict (not merely 'timed out'): opencode-notify EACCES after exhausting its 15-retry budget (runs 1, 3); codex-notify MODULE_NOT_FOUND (runs 2, 4, the latter also with a genuine codex-spawn process-missing failure and an opencode-notify PermissionDenied); one container itself never reaching RUNNING within its own 30s window (run 5, more likely general host load than the specific ag-* mechanism — this host had load average 1.2-1.5 and ~14GB swap in use during testing from many concurrent unrelated Claude sessions). This 0/5 tally on the CONTENDED host is an expected, explained artifact, not evidence the fix is wrong: fix (1)'s entire mechanism only takes effect once ALL palmux2 processes sharing the host's palmux-shared profile are running the patched binary, and this session's own operational constraints correctly forbid restarting either the live production instance (pid 1344297) or the orchestrator's own INSTANCE=dev rig (pid 247412) to test that — both remained on old, unpatched binaries throughout all 5 runs, continuing to strip 'ag-*' devices exactly as before. To isolate whether the FIX ITSELF works (as opposed to whether it can retroactively patch already-running unrelated processes, which it structurally cannot), a separate controlled experiment was run: built the patched binary once, started a second, fully-isolated throwaway instance ('instance B', no [agents.*] configured, own config-dir/addr/tmux-prefix, its own incus-container Workspace opened so its own ~10s scan loop actively reconciles palmux-shared) — i.e. instance B is a deliberately-constructed, FULLY-PATCHED stand-in for the unpatched production/dev instances, isolating the one variable (patched vs. not) that the contended-host runs could not isolate. Ran the real acceptance test (instance A) concurrently with instance B alive and ticking. Result: ALL PASS — codex-notify and opencode-notify each needed only 1 flicker retry (versus 12-15 in the contended-host runs), and all WS-attach spawn/stability checks passed cleanly. This directly demonstrates the fix mechanism eliminates the cross-instance flicker once both sides are patched; the 5/5 contended-host failures reflect an operational rollout gap (unpatched sibling processes still on this specific host during this specific testing window), not a defect in the code. Both tallies are reported separately per the orchestrator's explicit instruction not to blend them.
decisions.reference: sc4f091_verify_run{1,2b,3,4,5}.log and sc4f091_ctrl_experiment.log (session scratchpad, not committed — see the Story completion report for the full text); internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile_test.go's new unit tests corroborate the mechanism at the unit level independent of host contention

decisions.title: Backlog: full architectural fix (per-instance palmux-shared namespacing or a cross-process lock) explicitly out of this Story's scope
decisions.detail: This Story's fix eliminates the specific, common, and most disruptive pattern (one instance has agents configured, others sharing the host do not) without requiring any cross-instance coordination — but two instances that BOTH have DIFFERENT [agents.*] configuration (e.g. different resolved binary paths for the same logical agent across environments) could still disagree over device replacement and re-expose a narrower version of the same race. A complete fix requires either (a) namespacing palmux-shared per palmux2 instance/process (a load-bearing redesign of Sd44947's host-wide-singleton profile-as-mold architecture), or (b) a genuine cross-process coordination mechanism (e.g. a host-wide flock or a small out-of-process arbiter) around the whole shared profile, neither of which is Story-sized. Filed as a backlog item for a dedicated future Sprint; this Story's fix + the bounded pre-spawn readiness gate together are the maximal Story-sized reliability improvement achievable without that redesign.
decisions.reference: internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go Ensure() doc comment; docs/sprint-logs/Sd44947 (original profile-as-mold design)
